identifiedGap.currentClaim: The FBI traced the bomb to Jack Gilbert Graham, who had placed it in his mother’s suitcase after buying travel insurance policies on her life. He confessed and was convicted.
identifiedGap.finding: The cited FBI history does not support the claim that Graham bought the policies. It describes the $37,500 policy naming him as beneficiary as having been taken out by his mother at the airport.

proposedReplacement: The FBI traced the bomb to Jack Gilbert Graham, whose signed statement described placing the device in his mother’s suitcase. Agents found a $37,500 travel-insurance policy on her life naming him as beneficiary. A Colorado jury convicted him of first-degree murder.

sources.title: Jack Gilbert Graham
supports: Flight 629 departed Denver on 1 November 1955 and all 44 people aboard died.
The investigation located the explosion in cargo pit number four and found dynamite residue.
Graham admitted constructing and placing the device in his mother's luggage.
Agents found a $37,500 travel-insurance policy naming Graham as beneficiary.
doesNotSupport: That Graham purchased the travel-insurance policies.

sources.title: Graham v. People, 302 P.2d 737 (Colo. 1956)
supports: The signed statement described Graham placing the bomb in the suitcase.
Investigators found the $37,500 policy at Graham's home.
The jury returned a first-degree-murder verdict and fixed the death penalty.
The Colorado Supreme Court affirmed the judgment.
doesNotSupport: A causal claim that this case created a particular later aviation-security policy.

claimMap.claim: Graham's signed statement described placing the device in his mother's suitcase.
Agents found a $37,500 policy on his mother's life naming him as beneficiary.
A Colorado jury convicted Graham of first-degree murder.
